Its test file additionally imports and exercises NoBackChannelError alongside UrlElicitationRequiredError, demonstrating the fix generalizes beyond the one subclass. #2555's __reduce__ is defined only on UrlElicitationRequiredError, so it leaves other MCPError subclasses with the same constructor-signature mismatch unfixed. #2478's _restore_mcp_error hardcodes an isinstance-style dispatch (UrlElicitationRequiredError -> from_error, everything else -> from_error_data) and reconstructs from the wire-format ErrorData rather than __dict__, meaning any future subclass whose state isn't fully derivable from ErrorData would need to be added to that dispatch manually, and it drops instance attributes not represented in ErrorData.

clusters.pick_reason: #3243 is the only one of the three that changes context.lock's type from anyio.Lock to anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1) (plus a second flow_lock for refresh/authorization transitions) — its own comment explains this is needed because httpx can resume or close the auth_flow generator from a different task than the one that acquired the lock, which anyio.Lock does not support (task-owned) but Semaphore does. #2858 (a rebase of #2660, closing #2847) and #3252 both just narrow the 'async with self.context.lock' block boundaries (e.g. #3252 moves 'response = yield request' outside the lock) while continuing to use anyio.Lock, so they reduce contention duration but don't address the cross-task release issue #3243 fixes.

clusters.pick_reason: Both add a rejection when a request id is already in-flight, but #3063 keys `_request_streams` via `str(message.id)`, which collapses JSON-RPC's distinct int `1` and string `"1"` ids into the same key (a numeric id can false-positive 400 against an in-flight string id of the same text, or vice versa). #3221 adds a `_request_stream_key()` helper that prefixes `i:`/`s:` to preserve the int/str type distinction, and also explicitly guards against a request id colliding with the reserved `GET_STREAM_KEY` ("_GET_stream") slot — an edge case #3063's simpler `if request_id in self._request_streams` check does not address.

clusters.pick_reason: Implements __reduce__ on the base MCPError class using the generic 3-tuple form (callable, args, self.__dict__), so any subclass's extra instance attributes (e.g. UrlElicitationRequiredError._elicitations) round-trip automatically via __dict__ restoration, with no per-subclass branching required. Its test file additionally imports and exercises NoBackChannelError alongside UrlElicitationRequiredError, demonstrating the fix generalizes beyond the one subclass. #2555's __reduce__ is defined only on UrlElicitationRequiredError, so it leaves other MCPError subclasses with the same constructor-signature mismatch unfixed. #2478's _restore_mcp_error hardcodes an isinstance-style dispatch (UrlElicitationRequiredError -> from_error, everything else -> from_error_data) and reconstructs from the wire-format ErrorData rather than __dict__, meaning any future subclass whose state isn't fully derivable from ErrorData would need to be added to that dispatch manually, and it drops instance attributes not represented in ErrorData.

members.title: fix(shared): preserve MCPError payload on pickle
members.author: MukundaKatta
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3262: MCPError (triggered via UrlElicitationRequiredError, tracked in issue #2431) is unpicklable: default Exception.__reduce_ex__ calls cls(*self.args), but self.args is set to (code, message, data) by MCPError.__init__ which doesn't match subclass constructors like UrlElicitationRequiredError(elicitations, message=None), raising TypeError on unpickle. All three PRs add a __reduce__-based fix to src/mcp/shared/exceptions.py; #2478 and #3262 even independently name their helper function identically (_restore_mcp_error), confirming they target the same root cause.

members.author: Zelys-DFKH
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: All three modify RequestResponder's cancellation lifecycle in src/mcp/shared/session.py (cancel()/__exit__), which previously sent an erroneous error response when a request was cancelled. #2493 removes that response-send in cancel() and correspondingly simplifies server.py's now-unneeded duplicate-response-suppression branch. #2514 targets the same cancel() code path to instead emit notifications/cancelled on timeout/caller-cancel. #2624 patches __exit__ to swallow the Cancelled exception raised during cleanup of an already-completed (cancelled) request — a downstream symptom of the same cancel()/__exit__ interaction. clusters.pick_reason: #3243 is the only one of the three that changes context.lock's type from anyio.Lock to anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1) (plus a second flow_lock for refresh/authorization transitions) — its own comment explains this is needed because httpx can resume or close the auth_flow generator from a different task than the one that acquired the lock, which anyio.Lock does not support (task-owned) but Semaphore does. #2858 (a rebase of #2660, closing #2847) and #3252 both just narrow the 'async with self.context.lock' block boundaries (e.g. #3252 moves 'response = yield request' outside the lock) while continuing to use anyio.Lock, so they reduce contention duration but don't address the cross-task release issue #3243 fixes.

clusters.pick_reason: Both add a rejection when a request id is already in-flight, but #3063 keys `_request_streams` via `str(message.id)`, which collapses JSON-RPC's distinct int `1` and string `"1"` ids into the same key (a numeric id can false-positive 400 against an in-flight string id of the same text, or vice versa). #3221 adds a `_request_stream_key()` helper that prefixes `i:`/`s:` to preserve the int/str type distinction, and also explicitly guards against a request id colliding with the reserved `GET_STREAM_KEY` ("_GET_stream") slot — an edge case #3063's simpler `if request_id in self._request_streams` check does not address.
